scenes.narration: Computers never get bored. Today we teach a program to repeat itself, as many times as we say.

scenes.onScreen: "Repeating with while": three numbered lines (1. while checks a condition before every round; 2. The loop body repeats while it is True; 3. Something inside must change the condition) and an analogy card: a sea wave: it keeps coming in while the tide is up, and it stops when the tide goes out
scenes.animation: Lines spring in one by one with a pop; the analogy card slides in from the right
scenes.narration: A while loop repeats a block while a condition is True. Python checks the condition before every round. If it is True, the body runs again. If it is False, the loop ends and the program carries on. Think of waves on a beach. They keep coming in while the tide is up. For the loop to end, something inside the body must change the condition. Usually that is a counter that goes up.

scenes.onScreen: waves.py: a counter that goes from one to three
scenes.animation: Code types in with key-tick; butter [HL n] highlight sweeps line by line with marker-swipe; explanation card on the right; faint indent guide lines
scenes.narration: [HL 1] A counter, starting at one. [HL 2] The loop line. While count is at most three, run the block below. [HL 3] Print the wave number. [HL 4] And now the most important line. We add one to count. Without it, the condition never changes. [HL 5] Back at the left edge, so the loop is over. Done prints once, after the loop finishes.

code.source:
count = 1
while count <= 3:
    print("Wave", count)
    count = count + 1
print("Done")

scenes.onScreen: The name count tied to a new int every round; after the loop it points at 4
scenes.animation: Name tags pop in with their arrows to the objects (value and type shown, no addresses); when Python reads a name the arrow glows and the object lights up
scenes.narration: Here is the picture after the loop ends. The name count is tied to the int four. It was tied to one, then two, then three, and each time the tag moved to a new number. The condition count at most three is now False, which is why the loop stopped. The old numbers are gone, and the tag is on four.

scenes.onScreen: saving.py: saving money week by week until it reaches 200

[HL 4] Add thirty each round. [HL 5] And count the week. [TRACK saving=220] After four rounds, the savings are two hundred twenty. That is not below two hundred, so the loop stops. [HL 6] Four weeks. [HL 7] Two hundred twenty saved.

code.source:
saving = 100
weeks = 0
while saving < 200:
    saving = saving + 30
    weeks = weeks + 1
print("Weeks:", weeks)
print("Saved:", saving)

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: forgetting to update the counter
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the Python error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. We forgot the line that adds one to count. Count stays at one forever. The condition is always True, so the loop never ends, and Wave one prints again and again. No error appears, because there is nothing wrong with the rules. Press control C to stop the program. Then add the update line, and the loop ends.

shorts.title: What is a loop?
shorts.hook: "A loop repeats a block of code."
shorts.script: A loop repeats a block of code. The while loop repeats as long as its condition is True. Python checks the condition before every round. If it is True, the body runs again. If it is False, the loop ends and the program carries on. Think of waves that keep coming while the tide is up. Loops let one short program do a very big job. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Repeat with while.

shorts.title: The counter
shorts.script: Most while loops have a counter. You start it before the loop, check it in the condition, and change it inside the body. Count equals one. While count is at most three. Print, then add one. Each round the counter moves closer to the end. When it passes three, the condition is False, and the loop stops. Three parts, one loop. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Three parts of a loop.

shorts.title: Watch the name move
shorts.script: Watch the name count. It starts tied to one. After round one it is tied to two. After round two, three. After round three, four. Each time, the tag moves to a brand new number. When count is four, the condition at most three is False. So the loop ends. The loop just keeps retying the same name, until it is time to stop. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Follow the counter.

shorts.title: The loop that never ends
shorts.script: Here is the classic loop bug. You forget the line that changes the counter. Count stays one, the condition stays True, and Wave one prints forever. Python shows no error, because the rules are fine. Press control C to stop the program. Then add the missing update line. Always ask, what makes this loop stop, before you press run? Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Control C saves you.
